name: Ceat Ltd
title: Ceat Ltd - 500878 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: CEAT standalone FY26 revenue rose 15.5% to INR15,215 crores and EBITDA crossed INR2,000 crores; Q1 FY27 raw material cost seen up about 15%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 18.2% YoY to about INR4,036 crores, with standalone EBITDA of INR587 crores (14.6% margin) and profit of INR283.6 crores. Management flagged a steep raw material cost spike entering Q1 FY27, driven by crude near $107/bbl, natural rubber rising from about INR190/kg to INR245/kg, and a weaker rupee at about INR94/$. Price hikes of about 10% in replacement are planned through Q1, with OEM and international pass-through lagging. CAMSO transition continues, with customer interface targeted at about 90% control by September 2026, and India capex guided at INR1,350-1,400 crores for FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR100.4 crores YoY; INR191.6 crores QoQ

segments.name: Replacement (standalone, Q4)
segments.commentary: Grew mid-teens; 2-wheeler grew mid-20s, truck/bus/farm low teens, PCUV mid-single digit. Share of business up about 0.5% in PCUV and about 1% in motorcycle in replacement.

segments.name: OEM (standalone, Q4)
segments.commentary: Grew about mid-teens; passenger car very high growth on lower base, MHCV low double digit in Q4 per CFO-stated figures. OEM grew 20%+ in FY26. Share slightly down in passenger car (under 1%) and motorcycle (about 1%).

segments.name: International Business
segments.commentary: Strong Q4 recovery with growth in mid-20s on volume basis; saliency rose from 19% to 20.4% standalone, and above 23% including CAMSO. Middle East was about 15% of international business and near zero in Q4.

segments.name: CAMSO (acquired)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue flat QoQ at roughly -5% vs Q3 due to fuel shortage in Sri Lanka. Still in transition; customer interface targeted at 90% by September 2026, upstream mixer and calender by March 2027.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 raw material cost increase estimated around 15%, possibly higher on replacement-cost basis, with a path toward about 20% by end-Q1.
Replacement price hike of about 10% vs March: about 5% taken March-April, balance 5% staggered through May-June. OEM index-linked hike on 1 July expected to be heavier.
International business pricing: 3-5% taken, another 5% announced, targeting about 8% pass-through by end-Q1 given 30-45 day order base.
FY27 India capex (ex-CAMSO) of INR1,350-1,400 crores, about 25% above FY26 capex of INR1,076 crores; Q1 limited to mandatory capex of INR200-250 crores.
CAMSO upstream capex about $20-25 million in FY27, on top of India capex; CAMSO value chain expected fully in control by March 2027, margin impact from FY28.

Replacement demand expected to moderate after price hikes; MHCV replacement high single digit near term, possibly low single digit; PCR replacement may improve from 1-2% to 3-5%; 2-wheeler single to high single digit.
Finance cost: debt kept near INR3,000 crores in Q1, with a slightly higher level expected thereafter. CFO said Q4 other income of INR62.5 crores is not sustainable.
Management expects normal margin scenario from Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation at 85-90% across categories, with planned utilisation above 90%.
Q4 FY26 capex INR407 crores vs INR200-250 crores per quarter earlier; FY26 capex about INR1,076 crores plus INR236 crores CAMSO intangibles in Q2.
Q1 FY27 limited to mandatory capex of INR200-250 crores, with scaling up once conditions normalise.
CAMSO upstream equipment (mixers and calenders) targeted for March 2027 at about $30 million estimated cost, of which about three-quarters in FY27.
Overseas entities and branches set up in Germany, UK, France and Poland; over 130 new off-highway SKUs launched.
demand_pricing: Replacement pricing: about 5% taken March-April, with 5% more planned for May-June; competitors' price increases are delayed and staggered. MRF reportedly took about 3-3.5% across segments.
OEM price increase is index-linked: low single digit from 1 April, heavier hike expected 1 July.
Demand momentum from GST cut (28% to 18% on most tyre categories) carried from Q3 into Q4 and continues into Q1; management expects moderation as 5-10% price hikes pass through.
Raw material pass-through: only about half of the steep RM increase has been passed on to date.

US tariffs: on-road tyres at 25% incremental plus about 4% original; OHT tariff reduced from 50% to 10%, with refund sought via a court order. CAMSO tracks (about 50% of US revenue) at 10%, with metal clips at 25%.
Freight costs up 2-3x in several markets, recovered via surcharges.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 15% RM increase is reflected in current commodity prices and what further cost increase is possible?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 RM cost increase could be about 15%, based on inventory and orders covering about 3 months, with replacement cost possibly higher. Visibility beyond Q1 is limited because the situation is dynamic.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cumulative price increase planned and how will it be staggered?
qa_highlights.answer: Replacement: about 10% vs March, of which about 5% is taken; balance 5% staggered over May-June. OEM index-based with a heavier hike on 1 July. International: 3-5% taken, about 8% targeted by end-Q1.

qa_highlights.question: When will CAMSO revenue ramp up and what are the margin expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Customer interface about 90% by September 2026; turnover and volume growth expected in H2 FY27, with aftermarket first and OEM from FY28. Margin impact from FY28, with the 25-30% value-chain margin currently sitting with Michelin during transition.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q4 volume growth and segment growth rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume grew close to 20% YoY in Q4; international in mid-20s, replacement and OEM in mid-teens to 20s.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Middle East exposure and FY27 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Middle East about 15% of business, near zero in Q4; Q1 order base looks good excluding Middle East, which is treated as upside.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and the CAMSO upstream capex?
qa_highlights.answer: India capex INR1,350-1,400 crores ex-CAMSO. CAMSO upstream about $20-25 million in FY27, which management says is above INR100 crores and additional to India capex.

qa_highlights.question: How is competition behaving on price hikes, and what is the replacement demand outlook for H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes are coming through but are delayed by some competitors. Truck bus radial replacement may slow to single digit or low single digit after a 10% hike but not turn negative. PCR replacement expected to rise from 1-2% to 3-5%.

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 raw material inflation (crude about $107/bbl, natural rubber about INR245/kg, INR94/$) with only about half of the hike passed through so far.
Replacement demand moderation after about 10% price hikes, especially truck bus radial; high H2 FY26 base.
CAMSO transition execution risk and margin dilution during the interim period; Sri Lanka fuel shortage impact on production.
Working capital rose to INR108 crores standalone (from minus INR31 crores), including about INR120 crores of GST credit balances; management aims to return to negative working capital.
Debt levels of about INR3,000 crores with higher capex may rise from Q2 FY27; geopolitical risk (West Asia conflict) affecting Middle East sales and fuel prices.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and demand momentum but cautious on Q1 FY27, with management describing the environment as turbulent and the outlook as moderating. Answers were detailed on pricing and CAMSO, but some points were left open, such as beyond-Q1 RM visibility and the exact CAMSO margin path.
key_quotes: So, price increase is an imperative.
The volume increase and the value increase can only happen, therefore, in the second half and not prior to that when Michelin is handling the customer.

Considering that quarter 1 looks a little challenging with respect to cash that we will be generating and the margins standpoint, we will try to keep our debt levels, at least in the current quarter, similar to the level at which we ended in the previous 3 quarters.

adds.what: CAMSO upstream mixer and calender equipment (about $30 million estimated cost)

growth.why: Management maintains full-year double-digit growth (FY26 standalone was 15.5%), backed mainly by about 10% replacement price hikes and 85-90% utilisation, with India capex raised to INR1,350-1,400 crores for FY27 and CAMSO upstream equipment due March 2027; no specific new plant capacity was quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 FY27 raw material cost seen up about 15% with path to ~20% by end-Q1, and only about half of the steep RM hike passed through so far, while Q4 FY26 standalone EBITDA margin was 14.6%; margin relief only from Q2 normal scenario and CAMSO margin impact not until FY28.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Utilisation at 85-90% with planned utilisation above 90%; CAMSO upstream mixers and calenders (about $30 million, three-quarters in FY27) targeted for March 2027, but no specific new plant capacity was quantified.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 FY26 volume grew close to 20% YoY and GST-cut demand continues into Q1, but management expects replacement demand to moderate after 10% price hikes, with MHCV replacement at high single to low single digit, while PCR replacement may rise from 1-2% to 3-5%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 85-90% with planned above 90%, and India capex stepped up to INR407 crores in Q4 FY26 versus INR200-250 crores earlier; FY27 India capex guided at INR1,350-1,400 crores, about 25% above FY26's INR1,076 crores.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management maintains only full-year double-digit growth (FY26 standalone 15.5%) and calls the outlook moderating, with Q1 RM inflation and visibility beyond Q1 limited.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 RM cost up about 15% (possibly ~20% by end-Q1) with only about half passed through, replacement demand moderating after ~10% hikes, and finance cost rising from debt near INR3,000 crores with higher capex.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Over 130 new off-highway SKUs already launched and PCR replacement recovery expected, but no specific new product launch dated in the call.

rows.label: Replacement and international price hikes pass-through
rows.why: Replacement about 10% vs March (about 5% taken, balance May-June); international 3-5% taken with target about 8% by end-Q1, and OEM index-linked hike heavier on 1 July.

rows.label: CAMSO value chain control and margin uplift
rows.when: customer interface Sep 2026; margin from FY28
rows.why: Customer interface about 90% by September 2026 and upstream mixers/calenders by March 2027 (~$30 million), with 25-30% value-chain margin currently with Michelin; margin impact only from FY28.

rows.label: Middle East recovery as upside
rows.why: Middle East is about 15% of international business and near zero in Q4 FY26; Q1 order base is good excluding it, so any recovery is upside, but West Asia conflict is a risk.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 delivery, demand momentum and the pricing actions, but cautious on Q1 FY27 raw material inflation and beyond-Q1 visibility; analysts probed the RM cost path, the staggered price hikes, CAMSO ramp and margin timing, and replacement demand after the hikes.

oneOffs.what: Passenger car OEM grew very high on a lower base; the brief does not say the year-ago quarter was disrupted
GST cut (28% to 18%) demand boost carried from Q3 into Q4 and Q1, described as moderating; a temporary demand tailwind rather than a one-off item

quality.why: Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 18.2% YoY with volume up close to 20% and international in mid-20s, so growth is largely volume-driven from the core business; however, the GST rate cut demand boost (management expects it to moderate) and a modest passenger-car low-base effect flatter the headline, while the brief gives no quantified one-off gains.
